content: Chlorthalidone is a medication classified as a diuretic, commonly referred to as a water pill. This medication works by prompting the kidneys to eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. In some cases, chlorthalidone may be prescribed for other medical purposes. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Chlorthalidone is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically administered once daily or every other day, preferably after a meal, such as breakfast. Taking this medication in the morning is recommended to minimize nighttime urination. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you need clarification. It is important to take chlorthalidone exactly as prescribed. Do not take more or less of the medication or use it more frequently than directed by your doctor. Continue taking the medication even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. In addition to its primary uses, chlorthalidone may be prescribed to treat diabetes insipidus, certain electrolyte imbalances, or to prevent kidney stones in individuals with elevated calcium levels in their blood. Discuss the potential risks and benefits of using this medication for these conditions with your doctor. Before starting chlorthalidone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to chlorthalidone, sulfa drugs, or any other medications.g., prednisone), lithium, diabetes medications, probenecid, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or diseases affecting the kidneys, liver, thyroid, or parathyroid glands. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor immediately. If you become pregnant while taking chlorthalidone, contact your doctor right away. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking this medication. Be aware that chlorthalidone may cause drowsiness, so avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate this drowsiness, so it is advisable to limit alcohol consumption. Additionally, chlorthalidone may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight, so take precautions such as wearing protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen when outdoors. Follow your doctor’s dietary recommendations while taking chlorthalidone. These may include engaging in regular exercise, adhering to a low-salt or low-sodium diet, and consuming potassium supplements or potassium-rich foods like bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice. If you miss a dose of chlorthalidone, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Some minor side effects of chlorthalidone may include frequent urination (which typically subsides after a few weeks), muscle weakness, dizziness, cramps, thirst, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, or hair loss. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects require immediate medical attention. These include a sore throat accompanied by fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe skin rash with peeling, or difficulty breathing or swallowing. If you experience any severe side effects, you or your doctor can report them to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store chlorthalidone in its original container, tightly sealed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly by consulting your pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Chlorthalidone is available under several brand names, including Chlorthalidone Tablets®, Clorpres®, Tenoretic®, and Thalitone®.
